definition: The observation that plain SGD, with no explicit penalty, is biased toward flatter and simpler solutions that generalize.
details: The observation that plain SGD, with no explicit penalty, is biased toward flatter and simpler solutions that generalize. A large part of why deep learning works at all, and why optimizer and batch-size choices change generalization, not just speed.

explainer.lead: Implicit regularization is the observation that plain SGD, with no explicit penalty, is biased toward flatter and simpler solutions that generalize. It matters because it helps explain why deep learning works at all and why optimizer and batch-size choices affect generalization, not just speed.

tiers.eli5: Even without being told to keep things simple, the training process tends to land on simpler answers that work better on new data.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tune optimizer and batch size knowing these choices change generalization, not only training speed. A pitfall is attributing gains to explicit regularization when the optimizer's implicit bias is doing the work.
tiers.paperLevel: Plain stochastic gradient descent, absent any explicit penalty term, is biased toward flatter and simpler solutions that generalize better. The known limit is that this bias is observed and characterized rather than a fully specified closed-form guarantee.

explainer.example: Two models trained with different batch sizes reach similar training loss but differ in test accuracy because the optimizer's implicit bias favored a flatter solution in one case.
